content:
Last month we conducted a poll where the overwhelming majority of 9to5Mac readers agreed that Apple should get out of the advertising business.

Ads have now landed in Apple Maps in the US and Canada, and my view is that they are just as distasteful as expected…

Apple previewed this back in March, telling us that ads would begin appearing in its Maps app at some point this summer. We caught our first look at them yesterday, and the company confirmed that the rollout had started over the past few days. All users in the US and Canada will see them within the next few weeks.

  • Before search: "Suggested places" in the search screen will display ads.
  • After search: ads will appear alongside relevant results.

The company says privacy is a key focus.

I'm sure that's true, but I still think this is a terrible look for two reasons.

Top comment posted by John Atkinson

The only reason I can think of that has nothing to do with ad revenue is that adding ads to Apple Maps could encourage more businesses to claim their listings. One of the longstanding reasons Apple Maps has lagged behind Google Maps is that many businesses either don't bother adding their information to the map, or let it go stale. This is less of an issue in North America thanks to iPhone saturation, but far more pronounced overseas.

The theory is that ads can serve as an incentive for businesses to upload their information, since they can then run ad campaigns inside the same app (or get their marketing teams to fill out all the details in order to run those campaigns). Do I really think that's why Apple is doing this? Absolutely not — this is clearly about making more money — but at least it has the side benefit of improving map data quality.

First, while Apple doesn't deliver personalized ads through any form of tracking, virtually every other app and website does. Most people will assume the iPhone maker does too — however unfair that perception might be — and it will hurt the company's reputation for protecting user privacy.

Second, it just looks cheap. Ads are a necessary evil in the app and web publishing ecosystem: they're how free apps or websites keep the lights on. But Apple doesn't need ad revenue to pay its bills: it already charges a premium for its top-tier hardware. Ads simply don't fit the brand.

I believe it was John Gruber who once compared in-app Apple ads to those obnoxious Intel Inside stickers on cheap Windows laptops. We of course understand that companies making affordable laptops need to chase every possible revenue stream, but we'd never expect Apple to cheapen the MacBook brand with the same kind of stickers. So why should we accept seeing ads in native apps on Apple devices?

My position remains the same: Apple simply has no business being in the advertising business.
